Hi Elena —

Thanks for the questions and the quick read of the MAP. Short answers up front:
- Recommendation: Start with Hosted for the pilot (fastest time-to-value, minimal infra work) and plan Dedicated for production if consistent QPS/latency needs or strict network isolation arise. Private is recommended only if policy requires customer-managed infrastructure (e.g., full on-prem PHI custody).
- Dedicated lead time: 4–6 weeks to provision and test reserved GPU pools (depending on instance family and region).
- Private ops: customer is responsible for network & KMS configuration; Redwood handles control plane. Typically 3–5 engineer-days of coordination to onboard and an initial on-site or VPN validation window.

I'll attach a short recommendation memo and a region-latency/cost snapshot. If we get a signal from procurement on the target region (us-east vs eu-west), we can finalize the MAP and pricing sheet.

Next step I propose: can we lock decision by next Wednesday, Oct 27, so we can start provisioning for a Nov pilot?

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: MAP draft & deployment questions

Looping in some implementation constraints from infra/ops to feed the MAP:

- Dedicated pricing: expect ~18% premium vs hosted for reserved capacity (commit 12 months). We can provide a blended estimate in the MAP workbook.
- Lead time: confirmed 4–6 weeks but if they need a specific CUDA family (A100/next-gen), add 2 weeks to source capacity in us-east.
- Burst strategy: recommend host+dedicated hybrid for first 90 days — host traffic can burst to dedicated when reservation saturates. This reduces initial commit size.
- Private checklist: KMS/HSM integration, firewall rules, and audit log forwarding (we require network egress for a control-plane heartbeat). That component is the usual gating item.

I'll add these bullets into the MAP spreadsheet and flag the pricing rows for legal acceptance.

-Vivek
Director, Platform Ops

Thanks, Vivek — that helps. A few items from security/compliance: we will need SOC2-scoped evidence covering access controls and audit logs before procurement signs off on Dedicated or Private. Hosted is acceptable for the pilot only if Redwood can guarantee data segregation and short-term retention controls.

Regarding regions: CardioPlus is leaning us-east for lower latency to our backend. If Dedicated in us-east pushes lead time beyond Nov pilot, can we run pilot on Hosted us-east and then transition to Dedicated in December? We'd like the MAP to capture that staged path and an explicit rollback/fallback if Dedicated provisioning slips.

Can you add the SOC2 packet and an explicit staged rollplan into the MAP? Procurement needs those as attachments when we present next Friday.

Thanks,
Elena

Elena —

Attached is an updated MAP workbook (MAP_CardioPlus_v1.3.xlsx) and a short "Staged Deployment & Rollback" appendix in the sheet named 'Rollplan'. Highlights:

1) Pilot (Nov 8–Nov 21): Hosted, us-east. No infra work required from CardioPlus beyond standard IP allowlisting and test tokens.
2) Production (target Dec 6): Dedicated, us-east. We start provisioning on Nov 3 (4–6 week window).
3) Fallbacks: If Dedicated provisioning cannot meet Dec 6, we extend Hosted with reserved burst capacity and a 5% credit applied to Dec usage (see pricing-term-sheet-v2.pdf).
4) SOC2 evidence: included (SOC2-scoped-evidence.pdf). We will also produce a short access-control attestation for CardioPlus during procurement review.

Ask: please confirm acceptance of the staged path and sign the MAP workbook by Oct 30 so we can start provisioning Nov 3. I've put a signature tab and a couple of acceptance checkboxes in the workbook for procurement.

I'll schedule a 30-min slot for Friday to run through the MAP if that helps (I suggest 10:00 AM PT).

Regards,
